## Design

### 2026-10-13 – Designed the main enclosure!

**7h**

Designed the main enclosure!
My objective is to design a robust, custom 3D-printable enclosure for the MAIN_WATERING electronic assembly developed in Week 1. Rather than using traditional GUI-based CAD, I chose a parametric modeling approach using OpenSCAD since thats what i have used before.
Design Requirements & Specifications
The enclosure is engineered specifically around the layout constraints of the smart watering PCB:
Enclosure Architecture: A two-piece clamshell design (top and bottom shell) featuring a uniform wall thickness of 2.0mm for optimal structural rigidity.
PCB Positioning: Internal corner standoffs support the PCB at a height of Z=1.595mm, leaving 3.0mm of bottom clearance underneath for traces and soldering joints.
Component Clearance & Cutouts:
Pin Header (J1): Precisely aligned clearance cutout at coordinate (157.5,-82.5,1.595)mm.
Tactile Push Buttons (SW_PUSH_6mm): Mapped housing cutouts for button access at:
Push Button 1: (157.75,-108.75,1.595)mm
Push Button 2: (177.0,-111.5,1.595)mm
Push Button 3: (170.5,-111.5,1.595)mm
Fasteners: Corner screw bosses designed for M3 brass heat-set threaded inserts in the bottom shell, paired with countersunk top-lid screw holes.
CAD Modeling Workflow (OpenSCAD)
Using OpenSCAD allowed me to treat the enclosure parametrically, making adjustments to wall thicknesses, clearances, and tolerances straightforward.
// Key parameters from the model script
wall = 2.0;               // Uniform wall thickness (mm)
clearance = 0.5;          // Internal fit clearance (mm)
pcb_t = 1.595;            // PCB reference height (mm)
standoff_h = 3.0;         // Bottom clearance for traces/soldering (mm)

The script modularizes the assembly into bottom_shell(), top_shell(), and a reference pcb_assembly() module to visually verify clearance before exporting STL files for 3D printing.
Next Steps
Modell the node enclosure + bottle holder.
